title: Piecemeal traffic attenuator with KV-lease and stream guard
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During multi-region failover tests we observe spikes in token-latency and partial stream disconnects when we abruptly shift traffic. Existing weighted drain mechanisms either drop in-flight streaming sessions or force expensive full-session rehydrates. We need a controller that can attenuate (gradually eject) sub-populations of traffic while preserving long-lived streaming sessions and SLOs.

Goal: Implement a piecemeal traffic attenuator that uses short-lived KV-lease anchors and stream-aware circuit plumbing to: 1) progressively shift traffic by small fractional weights; 2) keep in-flight streaming sessions pinned to their current processing plane until checkpoint/kv-snapshot or heartbeat; 3) apply circuit-breaker decisions at per-route granularity; 4) perform priority load-shedding for non-session-critical requests to protect p95/p99 token latency SLOs.

Scope: Controller + gateway policy + runtime hooks. Deliverables: design doc, integration tests in staging, canary rollout, perf dashboard panels, and a GitHub PR for runtime changes.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Initial spike analysis attached to Confluence (https://confluence.redwood/edge-failover/attenuator). Two reproductions: graceful drain causes p50 to remain OK but p95 spikes due to reconnect storms; hard drain drops ~2% of streaming sessions. Proposal: use ephemeral KV-lease per session to allow transfer window before handoff.

2026-02-24 - Liam O'Connor: PoC of KV-lease handshake completed on dev cluster. Design trade-off: longer lease lowers reconnects but increases time until traffic can be fully moved off a region. We propose configurable lease TTL per-customer tier. PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5328

2026-02-27 - Design review (Maya Chen): Approved on principal. Feedback: add explicit telemetry gating to avoid oscillation; use a hysteresis window for circuit triggers. Action: add 'telemetry_backstop' metric to dashboard and set default hysteresis to 30s.

2026-03-01 - Reliability (Diego Ramos): Load-shedding policy draft added. Non-stickied requests (batch embedding, low-priority streaming keepalive) will be shed first; sticky chat streams preserved until KV-lease expiry. We need a test harness to simulate 10k concurrent streams to validate p99 under partial ejection.

2026-03-05 - Liam O'Connor: Integration tests green on staging with canary 5% weight ejection. Observed p95 improvement on fallback region from 1.2s to 0.85s for control path; streaming disconnects reduced from 1.9% -> 0.3% after KV-lease handshake enabled. Next: implement per-route circuit config UI hooks in Console and prepare runtime-2.4 canary.

2026-03-05 - TODOs by assignee: finalize API shape for lease TTL, add per-customer policy override, add Grafana panels (slo_headroom, kv_lease_active, stream_preserve_rate), schedule load test for 2026-03-10.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can shift traffic in fractional steps (configurable from 1% increments) without global grpc/socket resets
In-flight streaming sessions are preserved during an ejection window until KV-lease expiry or explicit checkpoint completion
Per-route circuit-breaker triggers exist that mark routes for gradual attenuation based on p95 latency, error-rate, and CPU headroom
Load-shedding policy evicts only non-stickied requests first and maintains SLOs for premium tiers
End-to-end integration tests simulate 10k concurrent streams and show streaming disconnects < 0.5% during a 10% weighted ejection
Console surface can set lease TTLs and ejection weight; metrics displayed in runtime-2.4 release dashboard
